Burlington County New Jersey Inmate Lookup

If you need to locate someone in the Burlington County jail system, this guide provides comprehensive information about how to search inmate records, understand the arrest process, and access official resources. Whether you're searching for a family member or need specific legal information, a burlington county new jersey inmate lookup can be completed through several official channels available to the public.

How to Search Burlington County Jail Records

  1. Visit the Burlington County Sheriff's Office website or call their inmate information line to search the current jail roster by the inmate's full name or booking number.
  2. Use the New Jersey Department of Corrections Inmate Locator if you believe the person may have been transferred to a state prison facility rather than remaining in county jail.
  3. Enter the inmate's full name and date of birth in the search database. Results typically include booking date, charges, bond amount, and expected court date.
  4. If you cannot find the person in county or state systems, check the Federal Bureau of Prisons Inmate Locator in case they are held on federal charges.
  5. Note the inmate's identification number once located, as this will be needed for visitation, sending money, or obtaining additional case information.
  6. Contact the Burlington County Bail Bond Association if you need to post bail or arrange bail bond services for the inmate.

Bail Bond Information for Burlington County

If someone has been arrested in Burlington County, understanding bail and bond options is crucial for securing their release. A bail bond is a financial agreement that allows an inmate to be released from custody while awaiting trial. Most bail bond agencies in Burlington County charge a non-refundable fee of approximately 10 percent of the total bail amount set by the judge. For example, if bail is set at $5,000, a bail bondsman would typically charge $500 for their services. It is important to note that this 10% fee is kept by the bonding company regardless of the trial outcome.

After arrest, the inmate will be brought before a judge for an arraignment, which typically occurs within 72 hours of booking. At this hearing, the judge will review the charges and set bail or bail conditions. The judge may release the person on their own recognizance (personal promise to return), set a cash bail amount, allow a bail bond, or deny bail entirely depending on the severity of charges and criminal history. Having a bail bond agency contact information readily available can help expedite the release process once bail is set.

Visitation Rules at Burlington County Jail

  • Identification Required: Visitors must present a valid photo identification to enter the facility.
  • Visitation Hours: General visitation typically occurs on weekdays and weekends during designated afternoon and evening hours. Contact the facility directly to confirm current visitation schedules, as they may vary.
  • Dress Code: Visitors should dress modestly and avoid wearing orange or clothing that resembles inmate uniforms. Tank tops, short skirts, and revealing clothing are generally not permitted.
  • Video Visitation: Burlington County Jail offers video visitation options for those unable to visit in person, allowing remote connection with inmates through secure computer terminals.
  • Children Policy: Children are generally permitted to visit but must be supervised by an adult at all times and must follow all facility rules and dress codes.

What to Expect After Arrest in Burlington County

  1. Booking Process: Upon arrival at the facility, the arrested person will go through booking, where personal information is recorded, a background check is performed, and personal belongings are inventoried and stored.
  2. Medical Screening: All inmates receive a medical evaluation to document any injuries, illnesses, or medication needs and to screen for contagious diseases.
  3. Classification Assessment: Custody staff will assess the inmate's security level, housing needs, and any special requirements based on charges, criminal history, and behavior.
  4. Arraignment Appearance: Within 72 hours of arrest, the inmate must appear before a judge for arraignment where bail is set, charges are read, and legal rights are explained.
  5. Transfer or Release: Following arraignment, the inmate may be released on bail, bond, or personal recognizance, transferred to a holding cell, or moved to a permanent housing unit if bail cannot be posted.

How to Contact Burlington County Jail

Direct contact with Burlington County Jail can provide information about a specific inmate's status, visitation procedures, and other administrative matters. The facility maintains phone lines during business hours for public inquiries.
